distinguishing_features: Non-contact AC coil array placed in or around the melt hopper/transfer section to generate a time-varying magnetic field in the melt path.
Eddy-current repulsion of conductive non-ferrous tramp such as aluminum or copper rather than magnetic attraction of ferrous tramp.
Frequency/skin-depth tuning of the field to particle conductivity and size.
Two-stage separation with upstream ferrous capture and downstream non-ferrous deflection/collection.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to remove conductive non-ferrous metal contaminants from a recycled plastic melt stream before extrusion while maintaining ferrous tramp removal and avoiding filter or screen blockage.
parsed.viable_reason: The asserted eddy-current forces and accelerations ignore viscous drag and phase-selection in molten polymer, so 1 mm Al/Cu particles would not be laterally ejected through a 10 cm melt channel in the stated transit time.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the cited references teaches or suggests an in-line electromagnetic eddy-current separation stage for non-ferrous tramp in a polymer melt, so the concept is not an obvious derivative of them.
